summary: Run it as a single scored submit with no companion. It ports a Triton align that prefill already showed was bit-identical. Each T class is gated in prepare() on torch.equal plus a 1.05x cold-L2 graph win, and that prints its own in-situ A/B, so the per-kernel profile rows and the [align2] lines can be read even though the headline effect (about 0.1-0.2% geomean) is far below the single-run CI. Before building, fix one gap: prepare() must compile every NCH_P2 variant.
justification: A. The mechanism is plausible at bs=128/256. Master's _align_parallel_kernel has 33 programs, and each streams all T*8 ids twice with a [512,32] one-hot. At T=256 that is 2048 ids x 2 passes per program, which matches 6.9 us in master's profile (4.0-4.2 us at bs=128 in FINDINGS). The two-phase form cuts each program's work to one CHUNK, and prefill measured 69->9 us at T=3012, bit-identical. I read the ported kernels (muse_prefill_layer/.../align-two-phase-all-t-rega.patch) against moe's incumbents. Placement keeps ascending route order (pre-chunk counts + in-chunk rank). block_experts from e_of = #(seg_end <= b*BSM) agrees with the incumbent when experts have zero routes. local_ids uses the same mask. The sentinel/padding/placement stores are disjoint. So bit-identity on raw global ids with local_start is credible. The bsm enumeration matches the code: d32 sees 8 (T<=28) and 16 (T 29-32). v128 sees 16 (33-57 and 128-172), 32 (58-115 and 173-191) and 48 (116-127; the hypothesis says ~108, but prepare enumerates it anyway). v256 sees 32 only. The expected directions agree with TASK.md: each load counts equally in the geomean, and the align is about 0.9-2.3% of each touched row, so the predicted +0.3-0.9% per row is the right order. That is about 0.1-0.2% on the headline, well inside the +-1.5% CI, and the hypothesis says so itself. WEAKEST LINK: the d32 class. The incumbent there is one launch at 4.2 us, and the two-phase form adds a second graph node to work that is only 136-256 ids (2-4 chunks at CHUNK 64). Two minimum-size Triton kernels plus the inter-node gap on H200 cost roughly 3-4 us, so the 1.05x gate will probably leave d32 on master, and the decode_32 'up' prediction (the load with the weakest ratio) is the claim least likely to hold. A second link: the 2.5-3.5 us estimate at T=128/256 is extrapolated from prefill's T>=3012. At T=128 (1024 ids) launch latency rather than work dominates, so v128 may also fail the 1.05 margin. Either way the gate turns a failed prediction into a measurement of master, not a regression.
confounders: triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack / marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm: these set block_size_m (16 at T=128, 32 at T=256). That fixes PAD_BLOCK, n_blocks and cap, so the align cost depends on them. This confound is benign: the hypothesis compares at the same bsm the timed path uses and enumerates bsm from kernel_fn's own pick, so the measured delta is the align's alone.
align-parallel-per-expert-verify: this landed the incumbent at T>32, so the comparison is align2 against exactly that kernel. Nothing interacts beyond the comparison itself.

triton-map-align-small-m-port: this landed the d32 incumbent (_align_small). Its single-launch shape is the reason d32 is the hardest class to win, which is a property of the baseline and not an interaction.

w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m: at T<=32, _w2_atomic_self_check runs _forward. Putting _align2_setup before it (as specified) means the w2 mode is chosen with the align that will be timed. If the order were reversed, d32 could time an align/w2 pairing that was never checked. Keep the specified order.

Not landed but relevant: cuda-nvfp4-wgmma-rega-grouped-s5-copy-safe-bucket-gate is BEST.json (1.3727x) but is NOT on master (master blob 60dfe35d is 9080a71, measured at 1.3445x). It runs its own align at WG_BSM for 128<=T<=512. This run's headline must be read against master's 1.3445x, not BEST, or it will look like a ~2% loss. If the wgmma rewrite or restack-bucket-gate-on-master-align-atomic lands first, the v128/v256 classes only matter for buckets that fall back to Marlin, and the two edit the same _forward branch.
interference: No companion is warranted. Two things already disambiguate a gain or a loss: (a) the prepare() gate prints, per class, the incumbent us, the align2 us, the ratio and the equivalence count, measured interleaved in the same process as an in-situ A/B; (b) the submit profile reports _align2_count/_align2_place rows to set against master's 4.2/4.2/6.9 us rows. An ab-revert of any landed hypothesis would not make this clearer, because the change is a bit-identical substitute for one kernel at a fixed bsm. A control that isolated the count or place launch would not ship and would only repeat what the profile rows already show. The headline cannot resolve 0.1-0.2% in any case, and a companion would cost a second scored run without adding information. Read the result as follows: classes the gate enabled plus profile rows below master's mean a real (small) gain; all classes printed as master means the run measured master (an unproven or flat result, not a failure).
rules_flags: Compile coverage gap (correctness/timeout risk, not a rules breach): NCH_P2 = next_pow2(nchunks) is a tl.constexpr that varies with T within a class. For example, CHUNK 64 over v256 (n 1536-4096) gives NCH_P2 32 and 64, and over v128 (n 264-1528) gives 8, 16 and 32. Enumerating bsm and testing a few equivalence Ts does not compile every variant. The bs=33, bs=257 and skewed tests could JIT inside kernel_fn, and possibly during graph capture. Fix: in _align2_setup, after the gate picks a chunk, call _align_two_phase once for EVERY T in each enabled class with that T's kernel_fn bsm (cheap, dummy ids) and torch.cuda.synchronize(). Better still, compile every (chunk, NCH_P2, bsm) before the gate.
The gate is plain ints in state, branches on shape only, the count table is per-call scratch sized by T, and there are no host syncs, prints or try/except inside kernel_fn. All of that is compliant.
The prepare() budget is fine. The L2 flush buffer (256 MB) and 41 interleaved replays x up to 4 chunks x 3 classes add well under 10 s. Free the flush buffer before returning state.
No precision or weight changes, and nothing is cached from data. The sentinel/padding semantics are unchanged, so Marlin sees identical inputs.
open_questions: Does the d32 class pass the 1.05x gate at all with two launches over 2-4 chunks? If it does not, the decode_32 prediction is moot and only v128/v256 are tested.

Should CHUNK 32 be a candidate for d32/v128? At n=136-1024, CHUNK 64 still leaves only 3-16 programs, so a smaller chunk or fewer warps (ALIGN2_WARPS=8 is sized for prefill's 512-1024 chunks) may be what decides the small classes.

Merge order with the wgmma rewrite (restack-bucket-gate-on-master-align-atomic is queued): the v128/v256 benefit disappears for any bucket where wgmma takes over with its own WG_BSM align. Should a later stacked hypothesis point align2 at that path?
The headline will be classified against BEST (1.3727x, not on master). Make sure the reader compares it with master's 1.3445x and the per-kernel rows.
